title: SFT on a code instruction dataset with TRL SFTTrainer
code:
from datasets import load_dataset
from trl import SFTConfig, SFTTrainer

# Magicoder OSS-Instruct has columns: lang, problem, solution (verified via the HF datasets server).
ds = load_dataset("ise-uiuc/Magicoder-OSS-Instruct-75K", split="train")
ds = ds.map(
    lambda ex: {"prompt": ex["problem"], "completion": ex["solution"]},
    remove_columns=ds.column_names,
)  # standard prompt-completion format, see TRL dataset_formats

trainer = SFTTrainer(
    model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B",
    args=SFTConfig(output_dir="out/sft-code", packing=False),
    train_dataset=ds,
)
trainer.train()
notes: SFTTrainer(model=<str>, train_dataset=...) and SFTConfig(packing=...) come from the TRL docs; prompt-completion datasets are supported. Not executed locally (TRL main requires Python >=3.11, local is 3.9, and training needs a GPU). The dataset is GPT-3.5 generated, so check OpenAI terms and license before commercial use. Swap model for your base model.
verified_how: matched official docs on 2026-11-24; dataset columns checked via datasets-server; not executed

title: GRPO with a unit-test execution reward (MBPP) in TRL
code:
import re
from datasets import load_dataset
from trl import GRPOConfig, GRPOTrainer
from reward import run_tests  # from the subprocess reward snippet (code-reward-subprocess)

ds = load_dataset("google-research-datasets/mbpp", "full", split="train")
ds = ds.map(lambda ex: {"prompt": ex["text"] + "\nReturn only a Python code block."})


def extract_code(text):
    m = re.search(r"```(?:python)?\n(.*?)```", text, re.S)
    return m.group(1) if m else text


def unit_test_reward(completions, test_list, test_setup_code, **kwargs):
    """Called by GRPOTrainer with prompts, completions, completion_ids, trainer_state
    plus every dataset column except prompt (here test_list, test_setup_code).
    Must return one float per completion."""
    rewards = []
    for completion, tests, setup in zip(completions, test_list, test_setup_code):
        code = (setup or "") + "\n" + extract_code(completion)
        rewards.append(run_tests(code, "\n".join(tests), timeout=5.0))
    return rewards


trainer = GRPOTrainer(
    model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    reward_funcs=unit_test_reward,
    args=GRPOConfig(output_dir="out/grpo-mbpp", num_generations=8, max_completion_length=512),
    train_dataset=ds,
)
trainer.train()
notes: Reward signature (completions plus **kwargs carrying dataset columns, returns list of floats) is per the TRL GRPO docs; MBPP columns (text, code, test_list, test_setup_code) were checked on the HF datasets server. GRPOTrainer itself was not run locally (needs Python >=3.11 and a GPU); the run_tests helper was run locally. run_tests is not a sandbox, so run training workers inside a container with no network (see docker-hardened-sandbox). Reward hacking is possible: tests are visible in the dataset, so for real runs hold out tests the model never sees.
verified_how: matched official docs on 2026-11-24; reward helper ran locally; trainer not executed

title: datatrove MinHash dedup of code, local executor
code:
from datatrove.executor import LocalPipelineExecutor
from datatrove.pipeline.dedup import MinhashDedupSignature
from datatrove.pipeline.dedup.minhash import (
    MinhashConfig, MinhashDedupBuckets, MinhashDedupCluster, MinhashDedupFilter,
)
from datatrove.pipeline.readers import JsonlReader
from datatrove.pipeline.writers.jsonl import JsonlWriter
from datatrove.utils.hashing import HashConfig

cfg = MinhashConfig(hash_config=HashConfig(precision=64), num_buckets=14, hashes_per_bucket=8)
BASE, LOGS, TASKS = "work/minhash", "work/logs", 8
reader = JsonlReader("data/raw_jsonl/", text_key="content")  # code field name in your files

s1 = LocalPipelineExecutor(
    pipeline=[reader, MinhashDedupSignature(output_folder=f"{BASE}/sigs", config=cfg)],
    tasks=TASKS, logging_dir=f"{LOGS}/s1")
s2 = LocalPipelineExecutor(
    pipeline=[MinhashDedupBuckets(input_folder=f"{BASE}/sigs", output_folder=f"{BASE}/buckets", config=cfg)],
    tasks=cfg.num_buckets, logging_dir=f"{LOGS}/s2", depends=s1)
s3 = LocalPipelineExecutor(
    pipeline=[MinhashDedupCluster(input_folder=f"{BASE}/buckets", output_folder=f"{BASE}/remove_ids", config=cfg)],
    tasks=1, logging_dir=f"{LOGS}/s3", depends=s2)
s4 = LocalPipelineExecutor(
    pipeline=[reader, MinhashDedupFilter(input_folder=f"{BASE}/remove_ids"),
              JsonlWriter(f"{BASE}/deduplicated")],
    tasks=TASKS, logging_dir=f"{LOGS}/s4", depends=s3)  # same TASKS and reader as stage 1
s4.run()
notes: Adapted from datatrove examples/minhash_deduplication.py (which uses SlurmPipelineExecutor): same four stages and MinhashConfig values; swapped to LocalPipelineExecutor (signature confirmed in executor/local.py) and added text_key. Class names and args confirmed from source. Not run: datatrove needs Python >=3.11. MinhashDedupSignature has language=Languages.english by default, whose word tokenizer is tuned for prose, so for code consider a custom shingling or a different near-dedup tool and validate on a sample. Decontaminate against eval sets (HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench) separately. LICENSE: keep per-file license metadata and filter to permissive licenses (for example by SPDX id) before training; The Stack v2 does this by file license detection. PII: scrub emails, keys, and IPs (datatrove has PII/formatting filters; BigCode used StarPII) and honor opt-out lists.

title: Hardened Docker run for untrusted generated code
code:
docker run --rm \
  --network none \
  --read-only \
  --memory 256m --memory-swap 256m \
  --cpus 1 \
  --pids-limit 64 \
  --cap-drop ALL \
  --security-opt no-new-privileges \
  --user 65534:65534 \
  --tmpfs /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,size=16m \
  -v "$PWD/job:/work:ro" -w /work \
  python:3.12-slim timeout 10 python candidate.py
notes: Every flag exists in docker/cli container opts source (network, read-only, memory, pids-limit, cap-drop, security-opt, user, tmpfs, cpus). A near-identical command was run on Docker 29.1.3 with python:3.12-slim: the script ran as uid 65534, outbound socket failed, writes to the read-only mount failed, and writes to /tmp worked. Kernel shared with host: for adversarial code add gVisor/Firecracker and seccomp. The timeout is the coreutils one inside the image (not separately tested); also enforce a wall-clock kill from the outside (docker kill).

title: Unbiased pass@k estimator
code:
import numpy as np


def pass_at_k(n, c, k):
    """Unbiased pass@k estimator (Chen et al. 2021, Codex paper).

    n: samples generated per problem, c: samples that passed, k: budget.
    Computes 1 - C(n-c, k) / C(n, k) in a numerically stable product form.
    """
    if n - c < k:
        return 1.0
    return 1.0 - np.prod(1.0 - k / np.arange(n - c + 1, n + 1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from math import comb
    # tiny check against the exact combinatorial definition
    for n, c, k in [(10, 3, 1), (10, 3, 5), (200, 37, 10), (20, 0, 5), (20, 20, 5), (5, 1, 5)]:
        exact = 1.0 - comb(n - c, k) / comb(n, k) if n - c >= k else 1.0
        assert abs(pass_at_k(n, c, k) - exact) < 1e-12, (n, c, k)
    assert abs(pass_at_k(10, 3, 1) - 0.3) < 1e-12  # pass@1 is c/n
    print("ok", round(pass_at_k(200, 37, 10), 6))
notes: Ran locally on Python 3.9 with numpy: matches the exact 1 - C(n-c,k)/C(n,k) definition for six cases, pass@1 equals c/n, and the check prints ok. Average the result over problems. Needs n >= k.

title: Reward function: run code plus tests in a subprocess with limits
code:
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

try:
    import resource  # POSIX only
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
    resource = None


def _limits(cpu_seconds, mem_bytes):
    def apply():
        if resource is None:
            return
        os.setsid()
        resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CPU, (cpu_seconds, cpu_seconds))
        resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, (1 << 20, 1 << 20))
        resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0, 0))
        if sys.platform.startswith("linux"):  # RLIMIT_AS is unreliable on macOS
            resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (mem_bytes, mem_bytes))
            resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NPROC, (64, 64))
    return apply


def run_tests(code, tests, timeout=5.0, mem_mb=512):
    """Return 1.0 if `code` followed by `tests` exits 0 within `timeout` seconds, else 0.0.

    NOT a security sandbox: no network or filesystem isolation. Use Docker/gVisor for untrusted code.
    """
    program = code + "\n\n" + tests + "\n"
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        path = os.path.join(tmp, "main.py")
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            f.write(program)
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                [sys.executable, "-I", path], cwd=tmp, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=timeout,
                env={"PATH": os.environ.get("PATH", ""), "PYTHONHASHSEED": "0"},
                preexec_fn=_limits(int(timeout) + 1, mem_mb << 20),
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return 0.0
        return 1.0 if proc.returncode == 0 else 0.0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    tests = "assert add(2, 3) == 5"
    assert run_tests("def add(a, b):\n    return a + b", tests) == 1.0
    assert run_tests("def add(a, b):\n    return a * b", tests) == 0.0
    assert run_tests("while True:\n    pass", tests, timeout=1.0) == 0.0
    assert run_tests("def add(a, b:\n", tests) == 0.0  # syntax error
    print("ok: pass=1.0 fail=0.0 timeout=0.0 syntax-error=0.0")
notes: Ran locally on Python 3.9 (macOS): passing example returns 1.0, failing 0.0, infinite loop 0.0 (timeout), syntax error 0.0. NOT a security sandbox: no network or filesystem isolation, and memory/process rlimits are applied only on Linux. Use inside a container (see docker-hardened-sandbox) for untrusted code.
